title: K6-PerfFramework Test Plan
description: Defines a complete performance test: which journeys to run, how many VUs, what load profile, SLA thresholds, and execution mode. This is the primary input that drives scenario orchestration.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor IntelliSense (ignored at runtime).

name.description: Human-readable name for this test plan. Used in report titles, result folder names, and CI summary output. Example: 'Checkout Flow - Peak Load Test'.

environment.description: Target environment name. Must match a config file in config/environments/<name>.json. The framework auto-resolves the environment config and injects baseUrl, serviceUrls, and secrets. Examples: dev, staging, uat, prod.

execution_mode.description:
How user journeys are orchestrated:
• parallel — All journeys run concurrently, VUs distributed by weight.
• sequential — Journeys run one after another using startTime offsets.
• hybrid — Mix parallel and sequential groups (requires hybrid_groups).
Most common: 'parallel' for load tests, 'sequential' for workflow chains.

global_load_profile.description: Default load profile applied to all journeys unless overridden per-journey. Defines the k6 executor type, VU count, stages, and duration.

executor.description:
k6 executor type:
• ramping-vus — Ramp VUs up/down through stages (most common for load tests).
• constant-vus — Fixed VU count for a set duration.
• ramping-arrival-rate — Control request rate, not VU count.
• constant-arrival-rate — Fixed requests/second.
• shared-iterations — Fixed total iterations across all VUs (good for data-driven tests).
• per-vu-iterations — Each VU runs a fixed number of iterations.

startVUs.description: Starting VU count for ramping executors. Usually 0 for a clean ramp-up. Only used with 'ramping-vus' executor.

stages.description: Ramp stages for 'ramping-vus' executor. Each stage defines a duration and a target VU count. Classic load test pattern: ramp-up → steady state → ramp-down.

duration.description: Stage duration as a k6 duration string. Examples: '30s', '2m', '1h30m'.

target.description: Target VU count at the end of this stage. k6 linearly ramps from the previous stage's target to this value.

vus.description: Fixed VU count for 'constant-vus', 'shared-iterations', or 'per-vu-iterations' executors.

duration.description: Test duration for 'constant-vus' or arrival-rate executors. k6 duration string. Examples: '5m', '1h', '30s'.

iterations.description: Total iterations for 'shared-iterations' or per-VU iterations for 'per-vu-iterations'. For shared-iterations: all VUs share this pool. For per-vu-iterations: each VU runs this many.

user_journeys.description: List of user journey scripts to include in this test. Each journey maps to a k6 scenario. At least one journey is required.

name.description: Unique journey name. Used as the k6 scenario key, report labels, and SLA references. Must be unique across all journeys in this plan. Use descriptive names like 'checkout_flow' or 'browse_catalog'.

scriptPath.description: Path to the journey script file. Can be relative to the project root or absolute. The framework auto-resolves paths by searching scrum-suites/ if the direct path doesn't exist. Example: 'buyanimal_1_framework_lifecycle.js'.

recordingLogPath.description: Path to the normalized recording log JSON for debug replay comparison. Only needed when debug.enabled=true. Auto-resolved from the suite's recordings/ folder if omitted.

weight.description: VU distribution weight as a percentage (0–100) for parallel execution mode. All journey weights should sum to 100. Example: Two journeys with weight 70 and 30 = 70% of VUs run journey 1, 30% run journey 2.

vus.description: Explicit VU count override for this journey. Takes priority over weight-based distribution. Use when you need a specific number of VUs regardless of global profile.

loadProfile.description: Per-journey load profile override. When specified, this journey uses its own executor/stages/duration instead of the global_load_profile.

tags.description: Custom tags attached to all metrics from this journey. Useful for filtering in Grafana/InfluxDB. Example: { "team": "checkout", "priority": "critical" }.

noCookiesReset.description:
Per-journey cookie persistence override.
• true (default) — Cookies persist across iterations (like a real browser session).
• false — Cookies are cleared at the start of each iteration (isolated sessions).
Note: Uses clearCookies() from session.js in the lifecycle.

hybrid_groups.description: Required when execution_mode='hybrid'. Defines groups of journeys that run in parallel or sequential sub-groups. Allows mixing execution patterns within a single test plan.

mode.description: How journeys in this group are executed relative to each other.

journeys.description: Journey names (must match names in user_journeys array).

global_sla.description: Global SLA (Service Level Agreement) thresholds applied to all journeys. These become k6 thresholds on http_req_duration. If any SLA is breached, the test reports a threshold failure.

errorRate.description: Maximum allowed error rate in percent (0–100). Example: 5 = test fails if more than 5% of requests error.

avgResponseTime.description: Maximum allowed average response time in milliseconds.

p50.description: P50 (median) response time threshold in milliseconds.

p75.description: P75 response time threshold in milliseconds.

p90.description: P90 response time threshold in milliseconds.

p95.description: P95 response time threshold in milliseconds. Industry standard for SLAs.

p99.description: P99 response time threshold in milliseconds. Captures tail latency.

additionalProperties.description: Custom percentile threshold in milliseconds. Key must match pattern p<N> (e.g., p97, p99.9).

journey_slas.description: Per-journey SLA overrides keyed by journey name. These apply to the journey's scenario-level http_req_duration metric. Override global_sla for specific journeys that have different performance requirements.

transaction_slas.description: Per-transaction SLA overrides keyed by transaction name (e.g., 'tx01_launch'). These apply directly to the transaction's Trend metric. Use for critical transactions that need tighter thresholds than the journey average.

max_total_vus.description: Safety ceiling for total VU count across all journeys. The gatekeeper pre-flight check blocks execution if the calculated VUs exceed this limit. Use as a guardrail to prevent accidental overload.

debug.description: Debug replay execution settings. When enabled, journeys run in single-VU mode and produce HTML diff reports comparing recorded vs. live HTTP exchanges. Use for validating script correctness before running full load.

enabled.description: When true, switches from normal load execution to debug replay mode. Journeys run with minimal VUs/iterations and produce diff reports.

mode.description: Debug mode type. Currently only 'diff' (HAR recording vs. live replay comparison) is supported.

autoResolveRecordingLog.description: Automatically find the recording log from the journey's suite recordings/ folder. Set false to require explicit recordingLogPath per journey.

vus.description: VU count for debug replay. Usually 1.

iterations.description: Iteration count for debug replay. Usually 1–2.

reportDir.description: Directory for debug replay output (HTML diff reports, replay logs). Defaults to results/debug/.

failOnMissingRecordingLog.description: When true, validation fails if any journey lacks a recordingLogPath. When false (default), a warning is issued and the journey runs without diff comparison.

noCookiesReset.description:
Global cookie persistence setting.
• true (default) — Cookies persist across VU iterations (browser-like behavior).
• false — Cookie jar is cleared after each iteration.
Can be overridden per-journey via journey.noCookiesReset.
